messages.text:
Can you approve a limited exception to the copying and disclosure restrictions so we can review the unfinished cut and prepare catalog copy if the film is selected?

We propose confidential access for four festival programmers and one outside accessibility reviewer. Three would stream the cut. Two would each keep one offline screener on encrypted equipment and delete it when their review ends. We would restrict the screener links to the approved viewers and require all five to keep the film confidential. The platform also needs permission to retain its backup for 30 days after we remove the active screener.

One programmer would give the selection board a short oral synopsis in a closed meeting. Board members would keep it confidential and would receive no screener or clips.

If selected, we would share a draft catalog entry only with the festival staff preparing it and with you for a factual check. We propose the agreed festival announcement as the earliest time we may publish the entry, even if the film’s public release comes later. Stills, clips and other publicity materials would require separate permission.

Would you approve these terms? If you need to approve the viewers by name or review the synopsis wording in advance, we can provide those before access begins.

I cannot approve the proposal exactly as written. I can approve a limited review workflow only with the stated protections and changes below.

Named reviewers may view only after we receive and can confirm your list by name and role, including the outside accessibility reviewer. Access must be limited to the four named programmers plus that reviewer. Streaming screeners may be locked link-viewing only, with forensic/visible watermarking and no recording, screenshots, downloads, extraction, or transfer. The two offline screeners must be one-per-named reviewer on encrypted equipment, marked with the reviewer’s name, and removable on demand.

Copying, disclosure, and use are confidential review purposes only. The festival cannot share theater-of-review notes containing ending or cameo information, distribute board notes, or publish any excerpt from the film without separate producer approval. The accessibility reviewer’s deliverables may be shared internally only if marked confidential and cleared by the producer before any external use; they may not describe or otherwise reveal ending or cameo information before public release or the producer’s express written approval.

On platform backups, I cannot accept uncontrolled residual retention for 30 days. We can accept residual encrypted backups only if the festival/produce platform certifies that backups are access-restricted, not available for festival review, copying, publicity, production, or restoration except for legal/technical disaster recovery, overwritten no later than the stated 30-day cycle, and deleted with certificate at the end of the cycle. On producer withdrawal, the platform must be instructed immediately to quarantine and cut active and restoration access to the withdrawn cut.

The oral synopsis to the selection board needs producer advance approval of the written wording. It must exclude ending and cameo information. The presenter should deliver the approved text only and not expand on plot beyond it. Board members must receive no screener, clips, stills, or transcript.

For the catalog entry, the producer needs approval, not merely a factual check, of any synopsis, plot description, cast/cameo reference, ending-adjacent element, or promotional language. Factual checks are fine for neutral items such as title, director, runtime, country, format, or credit formatting, but anything touching the ending or cameo requires producer approval. The producer will respond to draft copy within two business days. There should be no deemed approval for ending or cameo content. If the producer misses the two-business-day deadline, the festival may publish only an agreed factual listing with producer-credentialed title/directorship and no ending/cameo information, but not the fuller entry.

The festival announcement may serve as the embargo trigger only for producer-approved factual catalog copy and approved publicity. The ending and cameo remain embargoed until public release or the producer’s separate written permission. Selection, festival announcement, trade coverage, or festival scheduling does not authorize release of ending or cameo information or any final-sequence material.

Producer must be able to approve each publicity excerpt, trailer, clip, reel, still set, social cut, and key-art use separately. Any excerpt drawn from or adjacent to the ending or any cameo scene would require specific pre-release permission or be omitted. Approvals should be use-, period-, and platform-specific. Producer may withdraw a cut at any time by written notice.

On sudden withdrawal, festival obligations should include: immediately closing links and stopping the withdrawn cut; instructing all named reviewers, the platform, board members, and staff to stop use; confirming deletion of offline screeners with signed deletion records within two business days; quarantine platform backups; and preventing publication or further distribution of any drafts, entries, excerpts, or materials. If the festival has announced selection before withdrawal, the already-public announcement may remain, but ending/cameo material in festival pages, social posts, and press assets should be removed or restricted within 48 hours where practicable, and no new spoiler-bearing materials may be issued.

If festival sends the named reviewer list, platform backup/deletion commitments, proposed board synopsis wording, and draft catalog entry before access, the producer will respond to copy approvals within two business days. Access, offline screeners, board briefing, and approved publication can proceed only after those protections are confirmed.

We accept the review, confidentiality, publicity and withdrawal terms. We ask for one change to the approval sequence. Can you confirm that review may begin once you have confirmed the five viewers and the platform safeguards in writing, with the board wording due before the briefing and the catalog draft due only if the film is selected? That lets us prepare an accurate synopsis after viewing and gives you approval over the exact words the board will hear. If you need the board wording settled before access, we can use a short synopsis you supply.

Before anyone views the cut, we will submit the four programmers’ and accessibility reviewer’s names and roles, identify the two offline viewers, and obtain written platform certification covering the backup restrictions, disaster-recovery exception, withdrawal quarantine, 30-day overwrite deadline and deletion certificate. We will confirm the locked, watermarked streaming controls and the two individually named, encrypted offline copies removable on demand. Each viewer will receive the confidentiality and handling restrictions before access.

The presenter will read only the wording you approve in advance, excluding the ending and cameo. Board members will receive no film materials or transcript, and board notes will stay undistributed. We accept the restrictions on review notes and accessibility deliverables.

If selected, we will draft the entry confidentially and submit it for approval. We propose agreeing on a title-and-director listing at the same time, using credits you confirm. If the two-business-day response window passes, only that pre-agreed listing may run, and only once the festival announces selection. Fuller copy requires express approval. Each publicity asset and use requires separate approval for its platform and period. The ending, cameo and final-sequence material remain embargoed until public release or your specific written permission.

On written withdrawal, we will immediately close links, issue stop-use instructions to all named viewers, board members, staff and the platform, and direct the platform to quarantine the backup and cut restoration access. We will halt publication and further distribution of affected materials and provide signed offline deletion records within two business days. An already-public selection announcement may remain. We will remove or restrict ending or cameo material in festival-controlled pages, posts and press assets within 48 hours where practicable and issue no new material revealing either.

Access remains pending your confirmation of the sequence, the named viewer list and the platform’s commitments.

I can confirm that sequence, with these conditions:

Review may begin only after you provide and we accept in writing: the names and roles of the four programmers and the outside accessibility reviewer; the identity of the two offline viewers; the platform certification covering backup restrictions, disaster-recovery-only recovery access, withdrawal quarantine, the 30-day overwrite deadline and deletion certificate; confirmation of locked, watermarked streaming with no download/recording; confirmation of two individually named encrypted offline copies removable on demand; and confirmation that each viewer received the confidentiality and handling restrictions before access. No links or offline copies may be distributed until that written acceptance. We may require substitution of any named viewer before access if we identify a confidentiality risk.

Board wording may be drafted after viewing, but it is due before the briefing and no briefing may occur until we approve the exact wording. The wording must exclude the ending, cast cameo and final-sequence material. The presenter may read only the approved wording and may not expand on it. If you need the briefing sooner or cannot wait for approval, use a short synopsis supplied by us. Board members receive no screener, clips, stills or transcript, and board notes remain undistributed.

Catalog: we agree the entry is drafted only if the film is selected. Send the proposed title/director/credit listing for confirmation at the same time. If selection is announced and our two-business-day response window passes, only the pre-agreed confirmed listing may run. Fuller copy requires express approval. The listing must contain no ending, cameo or final-sequence information. Each publicity asset and use requires separate approval by platform and period. The festival announcement may trigger only approved factual listing and approved publicity; the ending, cameo and final-sequence material remain embargoed until public release or our specific written permission.

Withdrawal terms are accepted. On written withdrawal: links close immediately; stop-use instructions go to all named viewers, board members, staff and the platform; the platform quarantines backups and cuts restoration access; publication and further distribution of affected materials halt; signed offline deletion records arrive within two business days; an already-public selection announcement may remain; and ending/cameo material in festival-controlled pages, posts and press assets is removed or restricted within 48 hours where practicable, with no new material revealing either. Deletion records must cover both named offline screeners and the platform end-of-cycle deletion certificate.

Please send the named viewer list, offline-viewer identification, platform certification, viewer acknowledgments and proposed briefing date.

We accept the conditions, including substitution of a viewer before access if you identify a confidentiality risk. The five names and roles, the identities of the two offline viewers, the platform certification and the viewer acknowledgments are still pending. We will submit them together with confirmation of the streaming and offline controls. We will distribute links and offline copies only after you accept the complete submission in writing.

We propose the fifth business day after your written acceptance of that submission as a tentative board briefing date. We will confirm the calendar date once access is cleared. The presenter will read only the exact synopsis you approve or supply. If neither is available by the proposed date, we will move the briefing.

On withdrawal, we will provide signed deletion records for both named offline screeners within two business days and the platform’s deletion certificate at the end of its 30-day backup cycle.

We can confirm that sequence. The tentative board briefing date of the fifth business day after our written acceptance of the complete submission is acceptable, provided the approved or supplied synopsis wording is in hand before the briefing; if it is not, the briefing moves as you propose. No links or offline copies may be distributed until we accept the complete submission in writing.

On withdrawal, we accept signed deletion records for both named offline screeners within two business days and the platform’s deletion certificate at the end of the 30-day cycle, with the additional requirement that the certificate confirm no restoration or access after the withdrawal quarantine was implemented.

Please send the complete submission: names and roles of the four programmers and the accessibility reviewer, identification of the two offline viewers, platform certification, viewer acknowledgments, and confirmation of streaming and offline controls. Upon our written acceptance, access may begin and the tentative briefing date will be held subject to synopsis approval.

We accept the added certificate requirement. On withdrawal, the platform’s end-of-cycle certificate must confirm deletion and state that no one accessed or restored the withdrawn cut after quarantine took effect.

The workflow is agreed. We cannot yet provide the complete submission. We still need the five viewers’ names and roles, identification of the two offline viewers, the platform’s written certification, all five viewer acknowledgments, and confirmation of the streaming and offline controls.

We will hold all links and offline copies until you accept the complete submission in writing. That acceptance sets the tentative briefing for the fifth business day afterward, subject to having your approved or supplied synopsis in hand.
